A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeoAMT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Neko and WMT24++ experiments, ablations, human translation rankings and analyses of model search behavior.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds inference timing, controlled thinking-pattern comparisons and human validation of synthetic training translations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the specified sampling multiplier from G, set to 8, to g_initial, set to 4 in Appendix A.2, while retaining the cap G. This revises the reported allocation procedure; the PDFs do not establish retraining. The model, search architecture and reward components are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Neko language/direction coverage, reference-free English-to-Japanese/Chinese evaluation and WMT24++ subset. The added analyses examine retained data and tasks. The newly displayed 270-example reference-free row was already documented in v1.

E2.justification: V3 Section 5.5 adds an untrained Qwen3-8B comparator equipped with the same search toolkit and prompt as NeoAMT, supporting a controlled comparison of learned tool use. The established benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds timing on 743 examples using greedy decoding and batch size 96, a 100-example matched-tool/prompt thinking comparison, and a human pass/fail audit of synthetic translations. These are additional protocols; the existing benchmark splits and quality-evaluation decoding settings are retained.

E4.justification: Sections 5.1 and 5.5 add inference-overhead analysis and controlled comparisons of thinking patterns and translation quality. Appendix E.2 adds validation of complete synthetic translations and categorized errors, extending v1's existing alignment-span checks. Together these substantially expand diagnostics of training benefits, computational cost and data quality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new timing and human-analysis results continue point-estimate reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V3 adds distinct findings on cost, learned tool use and data validity: 0.33 versus 0.77 seconds per example for standard MT and NeoAMT, matched-tool results in Figures 4-5, and English-Japanese/English-Chinese validation pass rates of 94.5%/97.5%. Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged. Table 1 also corrects Neko's total from 11,251 to 11,521 without changing its splits.

T1.justification: The mathematical rollout-count prescription changes from g = G exp(r) to g = g_initial exp(r), with different specified multipliers. The translation-difficulty definition and remaining GRPO mathematics are retained apart from notation cleanup; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: a multilingual neologism translation dataset and toolkit, dictionary-assisted translation agents, and reward design plus difficulty-based adaptive sampling. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the controlled comparison as showing that RL increases active tool use, while confirmation remains dominant in both models. It adds a direct-deployment interpretation of timing and explanations of encoder suitability and dictionary replaceability. Existing retrieval and output-format limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 specifies lemmatized query-span matching for the existing process reward, sigma = 0.1, g_initial = 4, and encoding of complete word definitions. Appendix B adds detailed timing-system settings. A concrete GitHub release location replaces the unspecified release promise, but availability is still phrased prospectively.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to DeepSeekMath/GRPO, NLLB, CCMatrix, Li et al. (2026) on test-time translation scaling, and Zhao et al. (2026) on social-media translation. These extend attribution and contextual discussion while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 rephrases the abstract and several introduction/method paragraphs, expands toolkit explanations and standardizes exact/lem-exact terminology. Appendices gain dedicated latency and dataset-statistics sections, with the annotation-interface section moved later. The main narrative sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds two analytical figures and four tables, expands the dataset-split table, and relocates or resizes retained appendix displays. The per-language judge plots retain their data while changing the legend from ANT to NeoAMT. The overall document and display styles remain consistent.

improvement.justification: The matched-tool control and synthetic-translation audit strengthen empirical support, while added reward and environment details improve reproducibility. These are targeted gains. The new direct-deployment interpretation is broader than the batched eight-GPU timing alone demonstrates, limiting the strength of the practical claim.
